points.description: Finds a valid non-constant pair (P, Q) (e.g. with deg Q ≥ 2) that satisfies P(Q(x)-x-1)=Q(P(x)) for all real x, and verifies the identity correctly.

levels.says: Proposes a candidate pair or base solution but verification is incomplete or contains errors.

points.description: Describes a construction that produces new solutions of higher degree from a known solution (e.g. composing or substituting into existing P, Q so that the equation is preserved).

levels.says: Describes the idea of increasing the degree but the construction is vague or not shown to preserve the equation.

points.description: Fully verifies that the construction yields polynomials satisfying P(Q(x)-x-1)=Q(P(x)) for all real x (the induction/step is proved).

levels.says: Verification is mostly correct but has gaps or minor errors.

points.description: Shows the degrees: iterating the construction gives deg P ≥ 2024 and deg Q ≥ 2, and concludes existence.

rubric.notes: Full marks need a valid base solution, a degree-raising construction, full verification of the equation, and degree conditions. Equivalent constructions and alternative correct solutions earn full marks. Only a non-constant solution found earns about the first point; an unverified construction earns partial credit.
